answer: A zephyr of new identities can flood an agent economy unless each identity carries weight. Give every agent a distinct data shard to hold, like a willow bending under its own load along a ridge: the network assigns each identity a random encrypted shard and later demands a Merkle proof of a random segment. A shard is bound to its identity key, so one disk cannot serve two agents. An honest agent stores one shard once; a Sybil operator running N identities must buy N shards of disk and answer N independent challenges on time. Storage scales linearly with fakery, so flooding stops paying.
